chunks: Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hakam, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, on the authority of Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There was a small booklet in the cover (thong) of the sword of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What was in that booklet?' He said: 'It was the letters, each of which opens up a thousand letters.' They said: Abi Basir said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Only two of those letters have been revealed/interpreted until now.'

key_terms.الْحُرُوفُ: the letters (of the alphabet or divine codes)
key_terms.ذُؤَابَةِ: the thong or strap of a sword sheath

ai.seo_question: What was written in the booklet found in the Prophet's sword?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the concept of *Ihata* (comprehensive divine knowledge) encoded within the Prophet’s sword, where each letter serves as a key to unlock a thousand layers of esoteric meaning. The statement that only two letters have emerged 'until now' reflects the Shia scholarly view of the gradual unfolding of divine secrets through the Imams, culminating in the final Imam, while the rest remain in reserve. This underscores the continuity of spiritual authority and the depth of the Quranic text beyond its apparent literalism.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-32 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father, Muhammad ibn al-Hassan and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hikam, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Hamzih, on the authority of Abi Basir that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “There was a booklet in the cover of the sword of God’s Prophet (MGB).”

Abi Basir asked Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “What was written in that booklet?” The Imam (MGB) replied, “There were letters each of which opened up to one-thousand letters.”Abi Basir added, “Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “Only the interpretation of two of those letters has become clear up until now.”
